analysis:
This batch holds only documentation and changelog changes: two new changelog.d markdown files and a one-row edit to the `stop` row of the request-parameter table in docs/architecture/inference.md (line 1846). No executable source is in the batch, so I could not inspect the Swift implementation the docs describe (`StopHoldback`, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, `ReasoningStopScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`).

The documented behavior change is that client `stop` sequences now match only the answer/content channel. For GPT-OSS that is the Harmony `final` message. For Gemma 4 and `<think>` models, reasoning and tool-call spans are excluded. Tool-call frames are never cut. Leading whitespace before the answer cannot complete a stop sequence on its own. Native block-engine requests (diffusion Gemma) keep whole-output matching.

Threat-model relevance is limited. The change affects availability and correctness of the stop-string feature (finish_reason and empty content), not the TB-002 E2E encryption path (T-008 fail-closed) or the prefix-cache assets (T-041, A-001). A reviewer of the Swift diff should check three things:
- Stop matching must not leak or truncate in a way that exposes withheld reasoning or tool-call text in plaintext.
- The scope must be replayed consistently when the reported stop sequence is emitted.
- Held-back text must not be emitted unencrypted on any failure path.

The docs make no claims that conflict with the threat model. No regressions were identified in the supplied units. The Swift source is out of this batch, so verification of the code behavior is a remaining integration question.
